messages:
Mira: kicking off coverage sweep for the new ravena-liteq int4 onboarding. focus: funcall parse success across temps + streaming vs non-stream.
Arjun: what's the job setup? cluster, quant bits, sample size?
Mira: 2 GPUs (dedicated canary), quantized 4-bit and 8-bit; sample 1k convs from the canary prompt set; temps [0.0,0.3,0.7]; stream/non-stream; batch sizes 1 and 4.
Javi: running schema-coverage-checker v0.3 on outputs, collecting parse_failure_class tags and token-boundary fingerprints.
bench-bot: job 1805550000-1 started on canary-pool
Mira: initial pass numbers: parse_success_rate -> int8 non-stream 97.8%, int4 non-stream 86.4%; int4 stream 78.1% (yikes).
Tess: is this a streaming chunk boundary problem or model output entropy change after quantization?
Mira: logs show many cases where a quoted string in a tool args gets split mid-token and we emit a premature chunk. example payload excerpt:
```
{ "tool_call": { "name": "create_ticket", "args": "{\"title\": \"Crash while saving\", \"desc\": \"stacktrace...\"}" } }
```
Arjun: that looks like streaming chunking split a string literal; client-side parser can't reassemble unless we provide framing.
Javi: hypothesis: quantization changes tokenization probabilities so the model is more likely to emit closing quotes later -> makes split points different.
Mira: tried two mitigations: 1) strict-emit (buffer until output parses as valid JSON) and 2) soft-coalesce (on chunk boundary, if last token looks like mid-string, hold recent tokens up to 32 bytes).
bench-bot: strict-emit run 1805550000-S1 started
Mira: strict-emit results: int4 stream parse_success_rate rose to 91.2% but median latency +65ms and 95p latency +220ms. retry_budget utilization dropped from 2.3% -> 0.7%.
Tess: product question: is 91% good enough for streaming real-time UX? what's fallback rate?
Mira: fallback to non-stream or to int8 variant was used for 0.6% of requests in this run. cost delta ~+3% due to retries and extra tokens.
Lin: oncall: any API error spikes? saw small bump in 5xx during strict-emit warmup window. details in logs?
Mira: transient memory pressure on canary node during strict-emit buffering — fixed by increasing per-worker buffer limit.
Javi: additional finding: long tool args (>=120 chars) are ~3x more likely to be split in int4 stream than int8, and we see malformed trailing commas in arrays from int4 non-stream in ~0.4% of samples. opened a separate ticket for model byte-level cleanup.
Mira: plan of record: 1) add streaming heuristics: coalesce mid-string, delimiter-aware flush, and optional strict-emit flag per customer tier; 2) re-run int4 calibration with kernel padding to stabilize token-level outputs; 3) expand eval set with synthetic long-arg prompts to cover stress cases.
Tess: propose gating strict-emit behind "dedicated" and "enterprise" tiers, and expose a "latency vs parse-safety" knob in Console.
Arjun: infra: queued a nightly canary sweep at 11pm PT to measure parse_success_rate and p95 latency across modes. bench-bot: job 1805550000-2 queued for 23:00 PT.
bench-bot: job 1805550360 completed: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-canary/1805550000/artifacts (schema coverage report + token fingerprints)
Mira: final note: int4 non-stream still has a small class of outputs with trailing commas in arrays — JIRA RW-1234 created and assigned to research.
Tess: great summary — we'll review artifacts tomorrow and decide rollout policy. :eyes:
